summary: 1963 steel fire tower on Backbone Mountain in Monongahela NF, Tucker County, WV, replacing the state's 1922 Backbone tower; climbable to just below the closed cab.

facts.design: Steel tower with 133 steps up to a closed cab, at about 3,736 ft elevation

staffing.status: register visit reports disagree: 'No' on one undated visit, 'Sometimes' on a July 31, 2019 visit; no fire-watch history found in the sources read

access.note: Road open when roads are snow-free, most of the year by dirt road; climb 133 steps to just below the closed cab. Travel guide says mid-April to December.

visit.trail_note: Drive Forest Road 717 to the parking lot below the tower, then climb the 133 steps; the cab is closed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A travel guide says the state's first fire tower was built around 1916 but gives 1922 for Olson itself. The Forest Service dates the first fire tower in the state, on Backbone Mountain, to 1922, and the register dates Olson to 1963. The story follows 1922 and 1963 and reports the guide's 1916 line as the guide's own claim.

The register's staffing field reads 'No' on one visit report and 'Sometimes' on a July 31, 2019 visit. No narrative source read names a fire the tower spotted, so the story reports the register's answers and makes no further staffing claim.
Wikipedia says the whole walkway to the top is accessible; the Forest Service says visitors may climb to just below the closed cab. The story follows the Forest Service page.
The Forest Service ties access to snow-free roads; the travel guide says mid-April to December. The story reports the Forest Service rule and notes the travel guide's window.

notes_for_editor: Built date (1963, Backbone 1922) and elevation agree across the Forest Service, NHLR and Wikipedia. Current condition rests on one undated NHLR visit report. The register's staffing field has mixed visit answers ('No' on one visit, 'Sometimes' on a July 31, 2019 visit); both are now quoted and reported in the story. Access comes from the Forest Service page. One WebSearch via websearch.py; four page reads. No photos. No rental listed for Olson in the sources read.
